hints.title: Negate what a liar actually says
hints.body: A truth-teller has only liar neighbours. For a liar, “all my neighbours are liars” is false, so at least one neighbour is a truth-teller.
hints.recap: Truth-tellers cannot touch; every liar needs a truth-teller next to it.
hints.pitfall: A liar does not have to be surrounded entirely by truth-tellers. Diagonal contact does not count.
hints.pause: Write these two local rules beside a blank <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" display="inline"><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></math> grid.

recall.reminder: The negation of every neighbour has a property is that at least one neighbour fails it.

hints.title: Split on the centre
hints.body: If the centre is truthful, all four side-middle squares are liars. Each corner then has two liar neighbours, so each corner must be truthful. If the centre lies, it must have a truthful side neighbour.
hints.recap: The centre creates two exhaustive cases.
hints.pitfall: You may rotate the grid to place a truthful neighbour at the top, but must still cover the remaining choices.
hints.pause: Complete the centre-truthful case, then start the centre-liar case with a top truth-teller.

recall.reminder: Use cases that cover every allowed configuration.

hints.title: Finish the centre-liar case
hints.body: With the top-middle truthful, both top corners are liars. The left- and right-middle squares may both be liars, both truthful, or one of each. Reflecting the grid handles the two mixed cases together.
hints.recap: Only three side cases remain after symmetry.
hints.pitfall: A proposed grid must satisfy the rule at every square, including the last corner filled.
hints.pause: Complete the bottom row in each case and count the truth-tellers.

recall.reminder: For an extremal claim, rule out better values and supply valid constructions attaining the bounds.

solution:
Write T for truthful and L for liar. A T must have only L neighbours. An L must have at least one T neighbour, because the assertion that all its neighbours are liars must be false. Only shared sides count.

Centre T: all four side-middle positions are L. Every corner then has only L neighbours and must be T. This gives five truth-tellers:

T L T
L T L
T L T

Centre L: at least one side-middle neighbour is T. Rotate the grid so the top-middle is T; both top corners are then L. There are three possibilities for the left- and right-middle squares, up to reflection. Completing each using the local rule gives:

L T L     L T L     L T L
L L L     T L T     L L T
T L T     L T L     T L L

The counts are respectively 3, 4 and 3. These cases are exhaustive: the two side-middle entries are both L, both T, or different. Every displayed grid satisfies both local rules.

The minimum is therefore 3 and the maximum 5, each attained.

Answer E.
knowledgePattern: Enumerate consistent truth-teller configurations up to grid symmetry
